title: The Salt Summit
premise: When bush pilot Rosalind Oyelaran fishes a sealed chest from the Kessari River, she finds documents proving the drowned nation of Veyl was not destroyed by famine but by its own government — and that survivors' descendants still live at the river's forbidden source. Pressed by a ruthless salvage syndicate and an uneasy alliance of a disgraced archivist, a teenage stowaway, and a river guide with his own buried past, Rosalind flies and floats upstream through collapsing weather and betrayal to reach the hidden valley before the syndicate's gunboats do. At the source she must choose between exposing the truth — which will destroy the sanctuary's anonymity — or letting history stay drowned; she chooses a third path, broadcasting the archive while sealing the valley's location inside it, and in doing so finally claims a family she never expected to keep.
about_author: Ansel Fairweather is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent a decade ferrying supplies along remote northern waterways before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for river-soaked adventure plots driven by found families and moral weather.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A routine medicine run over the Kessari basin establishes her solitary life, her debts to the airfield, and her rule against attachments. She measures time in fuel gauges and river bends. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the reader learning what she's afraid of losing — nothing, she insists.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. After a storm, she spots something glinting in a gravel bar and lands to investigate: a bronze-bound chest stamped with Veyl's drowned-nation seal. Inside, waterlogged archives hint at deliberate destruction. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution; the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: The Man Who Reads Watermarks
chapters.summary: Archivist Tobias Wrenn's POV. In the port town of Lowmark, disgraced former royal archivist Tobias recognizes a photograph of the chest and comes looking for Rosalind, trailed by men he won't name. Emotional beat: desperate hope meeting professional skepticism.

chapters.title: Passenger Unknown
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She agrees to fly Tobias inland but discovers a stowaway — sixteen-year-old Nia, who claims her grandmother spoke Veyli and died waiting for 'the source to answer.' Rosalind can't bring herself to turn her out. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility taking root.

chapters.title: Gunboats on the Kessari
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. The syndicate's lead agent, Corvane, boards their moored plane at a fuel stop, all courtesy and threat, offering to buy the chest. Refusal means they're marked. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and immediate.

chapters.title: The Guide with Two Names
chapters.summary: River guide Emeric Sable's POV. Hired to take them where planes can't go, Emeric recognizes the seal — his own mother fled Veyl's collapse, and he's spent his life passing as someone else. He signs on for reasons he hides. Emotional beat: identity as camouflage, and its cost.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The river journey begins; a rapids nearly swamps them, Nia saves Tobias's satchel at real risk, and the group bonds around shared danger. Emotional beat: found family forming in the spray and fear.

chapters.title: The Burned Ledger
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Drying the archive by firelight, they decode a ledger showing Veyl's government sold its own people's grain quota and blamed the resulting famine on the river. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. We learn the syndicate's plan: control the source valley's resources under cover of 'recovery archaeology,' and why Corvane needs Tobias alive. Emotional beat: chillingly reasonable villainy — survival priced in other people.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. At a toll crossing, Emeric secretly signals the syndicate — trading information for protection of his mother's grave village downstream. Nia sees him. Emotional beat: betrayal born of love, witnessed too soon.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Falls Camp
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Nia forces Emeric's confession; Rosalind must decide mid-argument as syndicate scouts close in. She chooses to keep him — conditionally — because they need his river knowledge. Emotional beat: trust as a calculated risk, family as forgiveness in advance.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. An early blizzard traps them; the plane is damaged beyond easy repair, stranding them above the last navigable water. Rations shrink. Emotional beat: survival stripped to essentials, and unexpected tenderness in the forced intimacy.

chapters.title: Nia's Grandmother's Map
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Nia reveals a song-map memorized from her grandmother — verses encoding the route past the falls. For the first time the group has a way forward no syndicate chart shows. Emotional beat: inheritance as survival tool; the dead guiding the living.

chapters.title: The Portage of Bones
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. They portage through a canyon littered with Veyl's refugee dead, preserved by cold. Emeric finally speaks his mother's true name aloud. Emotional beat: mourning as reclamation of identity.

chapters.title: Corvane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Gunboats reach the falls via a bribed surveyor's route; Corvane takes hostages in a downstream village to force surrender of the chest. Emotional beat: the cost of the quest landing on innocents.

chapters.title: The Devil's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Cornered, Rosalind proposes splitting up: she'll surrender herself and the chest while the others run the source route. Tobias refuses to let her martyr herself; they improvise a riskier joint plan. Emotional beat: leadership learned — she stops measuring life in miles and starts measuring it in people.

chapters.title: The Source Gate
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Following the song-map, they find the hidden gate in the canyon wall and the living descendants of Veyl, who greet strangers with drawn bows and a test of memory. Nia answers in her grandmother's tongue. Emotional beat: belonging offered and almost refused.

chapters.title: Sanctuary and Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. The valley elders reveal they've known about the syndicate for years and plan to seal the pass forever, erasing even the archive. Corvane's force arrives at the gate. Emotional beat: safety versus truth — the same choice that doomed Veyl, replayed.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Gate
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. The valley's defenses, Emeric's knowledge of syndicate tactics, and Rosalind's repaired radio plane converge; Corvane is defeated when his own hired crews defect upon hearing the broadcast truth. Emotional beat: courage as collective act, not solo heroics.

chapters.title: Broadcast from the Source
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Resolution begins. From the valley transmitter, Rosalind reads the ledger to the whole basin — naming Veyl's betrayers and the survivors — while the elders encode the valley's coordinates into a cipher only the song-map can open. Emotional beat: truth without sacrifice of the innocent.

chapters.title: Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Aftermath: Tobias restored to his profession, Emeric reclaiming his mother's name publicly, Nia claimed by both blood and chosen family. Rosalind is offered a place — and a reason to land. Emotional beat: identity as something shared, not hidden.

chapters.title: Grounded, Finally
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Epilogue. Rosalind flies the supply run again, but now the miles have a destination; she banks over the source canyon, salutes it silently, and turns for home where people wait. Emotional beat: quiet joy — survival's price paid, and worth it.
